label: Lists
gloss: a list is many rows under one name; you count it, total it, or walk it one row at a time
why: A one-row lookup gives you an object; a whole-table lookup gives you a list (an array). You cannot read batch.invoiceTotal off a list - which row would it mean - but you can count it with len(batch), total a column with sum(batch, 'invoiceTotal'), or walk it with {{#each batch}} in a compose. At Beacon, the 2:30 PM run needs exactly those: how many invoices, how much, and one line each.
cue: if a field holds [3 rows], reach for len, sum, or each - not a dotted path
task: Summarize the batch: set count to the number of rows in batch and total to the sum of their invoiceTotal.
notes: len(batch) - how many rows the list has.
sum(batch, 'invoiceTotal') - add up one column across the rows (column name in quotes).
In a compose, {{#each batch}} ... {{/each}} repeats once per row.
A list shows as [3 rows] in the trace; an object shows as {...}.

checks.label: count is 3 (three invoices in the batch)
